core: Walk the premises. Check security, general condition, equipment servicing records and contingency arrangements (power, IT or fridge failure).
Check storage conditions, fridge temperature exceptions, recall actions and expired-stock handling since the last visit.
Review dispensing incidents, near misses, complaints and recurring errors since the last visit, and whether earlier fixes worked.

Consider safeguards for high-risk medicines relevant to this pharmacy. Sample records only when indicated. Reuse existing S8 stock-check evidence rather than recounting. S8 storage (Regulation 2026 s 122; Medicine Storage Standards Part 1): S8 kept only in the locked safe or strongroom, or a locked fridge holding scheduled medicines only; safe securely fixed and not accessible to the public; keys held by a pharmacist or in a separately locked receptacle only pharmacists can open; codes not given to non-pharmacists, changed regularly, and personal codes removed when staff leave.
Check that open Tasks from earlier visits and reviews are progressing. Open Tasks are listed at the top of this visit.
Supervision, communication, credential concerns and follow-up for staff. Detailed credential checks stay in Staff & credentials.
Ask how unknown prescribers and new patients are verified, and look at how a suspected forgery would be handled (NSW Health, Lost, stolen or forged prescriptions).
Ask where dispensed prescriptions, S8 copies, emergency supplies, urgent-use orders and wholesale or borrowing records are kept, and that they can be produced without delay.
Check any phone, fax or email directions were followed by a prescription, and late ones were reported after 14 days.

Ask to see the owing-scripts, uncollected-scripts and negative-stock reports, and compare a few wholesaler S8 invoices with the register (Pharmacy Council, Supporting resources for proprietor oversight).

Ask to see the recall notices received since the last visit and what was done for each (TGA PRAC procedure). The sponsor’s deadlines are theirs; the pharmacy follows the notice and records its response.

staged: Review missed collections, changed directions, prescriber communication, medicine security and open findings. Use existing pharmacy-wide S8 evidence.
vaccination: Check fridge temperature monitoring and data-logger review, vaccination incidents or adverse events, and any cold-chain breach or equipment failure since the last visit.
daa: Review DAA packing exceptions, medication changes, final checking and open findings. Check labels show the date packed and the patient’s date of birth, no pack mixes oral and external-use medicines, and third-party packs carry a reference number (Regulation 2026 s 136).

items.title: Prescription verification
items.question: Prescriptions (NSW Health): new patient with an unknown prescriber means the script is verified (contact details from another source; the lost, stolen and forged list checked); if it cannot be verified and nothing is suspicious, no more than 2 days’ supply and the script is kept.
items.guide: Ask how unknown prescribers and new patients are verified, and look at how a suspected forgery would be handled (NSW Health, Lost, stolen or forged prescriptions).

items.title: Prescription records (2 years)
items.question: Records (Regulation s 185; NSW Health): dispensed prescriptions, emergency supplies, urgent-use orders, wholesale and borrowing records, and copies of S8 and anabolic steroid prescriptions kept 2 years on the premises and producible without delay; paper S8 copies kept separately.
items.guide: Ask where dispensed prescriptions, S8 copies, emergency supplies, urgent-use orders and wholesale or borrowing records are kept, and that they can be produced without delay.

items.title: Phone, fax and email directions
items.question: Phone, fax or email directions (NSW Health): any script not received within 14 days was reported to Pharmaceutical Services.
items.guide: Check any phone, fax or email directions were followed by a prescription, and late ones were reported after 14 days.

items.title: Routine reports
items.question: Routine reports (Pharmacy Council, proprietor oversight): owing scripts, uncollected scripts, negative stock and wholesaler invoices against the S8 register looked at since the last visit.
items.guide: Ask to see the owing-scripts, uncollected-scripts and negative-stock reports, and compare a few wholesaler S8 invoices with the register (Pharmacy Council, Supporting resources for proprietor oversight).

items.title: Recalls and alerts
items.question: Recalls (TGA, Procedure for recalls, product alerts and product corrections): any recall or alert received since the last visit was acted on as the notice says, affected stock checked, and the response recorded.
items.guide: Ask to see the recall notices received since the last visit and what was done for each (TGA PRAC procedure). The sponsor’s deadlines are theirs; the pharmacy follows the notice and records its response.
